## TL;DR

Implemented the human-task “Mark done” modal with an optional multi-line completion report and fixed the activity reader so the report remains readable after it is written to the task file. The activity parser now joins `> ` continuation lines to their timestamped activity entry, preserving newlines and Markdown. Added a component test that opens the activity entry and checks the complete report text. The focused test and scoped RepoOS check passed; the review screenshot declaration targets the modal.

## Work and rationale

The original completion note control was a single-line input in the human-task drawer. That made longer reports hard to compose and read. The feature moves the action into a shared dialog, with a labelled multi-line textarea, Cancel and Mark done actions, and support for an empty report. The report continues to use the existing completion-note field so the task-file format and existing status flow remain consistent.

During review, the remaining issue was downstream display: the task-file writer represents subsequent lines as quoted `> ` continuation lines under the timestamped activity entry. `DebugPanel.vue` previously recognized only timestamped `- ` entries, so it displayed just the first line. I updated its activity parsing to associate continuation lines with the preceding entry and remove the quote marker while retaining line breaks. The entry’s detail view can then render the full report rather than a truncated first line.

Multiline activity content is marked expandable independently of measured ellipsis state. This matters because content with explicit newline characters is already longer than a single-line preview, and tests that do not perform browser layout measurement should still be able to open the detail view.

The change uses the existing dialog and global form/button styling conventions. No runtime package was added. The shot declaration captures the human-task completion modal from the task drawer using a fixture route and a click on the Mark done action.

## Approaches tried

I first added parsing for continuation lines and a component-level test using a task body with a timestamped activity item followed by quoted lines. The initial test fixture lacked a preceding section, so the component did not parse the Activity section as expected; adding a normal preceding section made the fixture match a real task file.

The next test attempt showed that the DOM test environment does not calculate the visual ellipsis used by the existing expandable-row behavior. I adjusted the expandability rule so an explicit newline makes an activity entry expandable without relying on layout measurement, then removed the unnecessary width mocks. The resulting component test exercises the actual row click and verifies the full multi-line content in the opened detail.

## Challenges and blockers

The main challenge was representing the real serialized task-file format in a component test and ensuring the rendered detail, rather than only the parser output, included every line. The first fixture and the layout-dependent expandability behavior each exposed gaps in that test setup; both were corrected before verification.

The scoped `REPOOS_CHECK_CHANGED=main repoos check` completed successfully. It waited for a shared Playwright slot during the rendered contrast audit, then passed. The check reported that tests had run on the remote validation runner and skipped the duplicate local test step; the focused component test was also run locally and passed. The earlier review handoff failures about screenshot target selection and a loading diff were resolved in the screenshot declaration before this round; the latest review finding concerned activity rendering only.

## Key learnings

Task activity parsing must follow the task-file writer’s multiline encoding, not assume every visible activity line has a timestamp. Continuation lines belong to the immediately preceding event and should preserve their original line breaks after removing the serialization marker.

Component tests that interact with content expansion should not depend solely on browser-measured truncation. Explicit multiline content gives the component enough information to expose its detail affordance deterministically, improving both accessibility and test reliability.

## Summary

The human completion report now has a multi-line entry flow, and its full contents survive activity rendering after save. Empty reports remain valid. The round-trip/display coverage checks the component’s rendered detail content.

## Files changed

- `src/ui-app/src/components/TaskDrawer.vue` — opens the shared Mark done dialog and submits the optional report.
- `src/ui-app/src/components/DebugPanel.vue` — appends quoted continuation lines to the preceding activity item.
- `src/ui-app/src/lib/debug-event-expand.ts` — treats explicit multi-line activity as expandable.
- `src/ui-app/tests/debug-event-expand.test.ts` — covers multiline activity expandability and verifies the complete report through a real component interaction.
- `src/ui-app/src/style.css` — shared modal/form presentation for the completion report dialog.
- `src/ui-app` task-file writer/parser test coverage — verifies multiline completion report round-trip.
- `work/1048-human-task-mark-done-modal-with-multi-li.md` — declares the review screenshot for the open modal.

## Tests

- `bunx vitest run tests/debug-event-expand.test.ts` from `src/ui-app` — passed (9 tests).
- `REPOOS_CHECK_CHANGED=main repoos check` — passed. Formatting, lint, build, CSS/theme guards, rendered contrast audit, task asset guard, and UI smoke passed. Test suite ran on the remote validation runner as reported by RepoOS.

## Shots

The declared shot is “Human task completion report modal”. It opens the task drawer on a human-task fixture, switches to a drawer tab without diff loading, clicks the Mark done action, and highlights `.human-done-modal`. Earlier screenshot verification failures were addressed by using the fixture and tab route that render the human-task action without a loading diff.
